proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
\nu=(A,(b_t)_{t=2}^T,v),
\qquad
\mathcal N=[1/2,2]^{\mathcal G}\times[1/2,2]^{T-1}
                 \times[1/2,3]^{\mathcal D},
\]
and set \(b_1=1\).  Thus \(\mathcal N\) is a compact semialgebraic set, and, with the fixed \(s\), every \(\nu\in\mathcal N\) determines \(\eta=(s,A,b,v)\).  This uses respectively the exposure-box, time-normalization, time-box, and treated-multiplier-box assumptions.

First note that the target is well defined throughout \(\mathcal N\).  The cells \((2,t)\), \(t=2,\ldots,T\), all belong to \(\mathcal D\).  Observed-share overlap and the exposure and time boxes therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
B(\eta)
 &=\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}s_gA_gb_t
 \ge \sum_{t=2}^T s_2A_2b_t                                      \\
 &\ge (T-1)\frac{1}{2T}\frac12\frac12
 =\frac{T-1}{8T}>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\theta(\eta)
=\frac{H(\eta)}{B(\eta)}-1
=\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}
  \frac{w^0_{gt}}{B(\eta)}(v_{gt}-1).
\]
The weights in the last sum are positive and sum to one.  Since the treated-multiplier box gives \(-1/2\le v_{gt}-1\le2\), it follows that \(\theta(\eta)\in\Theta=[-1/2,2]\).  Consequently, reporting \(\Theta\) outside \(\mathcal B_K\), as required by the finite-grid construction and the established finite-reduction theorem, always covers the target there and saves no length there.

For \(x\in\mathcal B_K\), exact product-Poisson sampling yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\eta,\kappa}(X=x)
 &=\prod_{g\in\mathcal G,\,t\le T}
   \exp\{-\kappa w_{gt}(\eta)\}
   \frac{\{\kappa w_{gt}(\eta)\}^{x_{gt}}}{x_{gt}!}                \\
 &=\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}
   \frac{\kappa^{|x|}}{\prod_{g,t}x_{gt}!}
   \prod_{g,t}w_{gt}(\eta)^{x_{gt}},
\qquad
|x|=\sum_{g,t}x_{gt}.
\end{aligned}
\]
At the fixed algebraic \(s\), every \(w_{gt}\), and hence \(M=\sum_{g,t}w_{gt}\), is a polynomial in \(\nu\).  Because \(\kappa\) is algebraic, the factor after the exponential in the last display is a polynomial over the field \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) of real algebraic numbers.

Write \(a(x)=[u_x,c_x]\) for \(x\in\mathcal B_K\).  Its endpoints are algebraic by hypothesis.  Positivity of \(B\) proves the equivalence
\[
\theta(\eta)\in a(x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(1+u_x)B(\eta)\le H(\eta)
\ \text{ and }\
H(\eta)\le(1+c_x)B(\eta).
\]
Both inequalities are polynomial inequalities over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).  There are finitely many \(x\in\mathcal B_K\).  The cited semialgebraic stratification lemma, applied to these finitely many sign conditions and the faces of \(\mathcal N\), therefore gives a finite compatible smooth semialgebraic stratification \(\{S_j\}_{j=1}^J\) of \(\mathcal N\), defined over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\), on each member of which every target-membership truth value is fixed.

For a stratum \(S_j\), let
\[
\mathcal F_j=\{x\in\mathcal B_K:\theta(\eta)\notin a(x)
                     \text{ for }\eta\in S_j\}.
\]
Compatibility makes this definition independent of the choice of \(\eta\in S_j\).  The preceding probability formula and full coverage outside the box now imply, for \(\eta\in S_j\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a(\eta)
 &=1-\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p^{\mathrm{fail}}_{a,j}(\eta),\\
p^{\mathrm{fail}}_{a,j}(\eta)
 &=\sum_{x\in\mathcal F_j}
   \frac{\kappa^{|x|}}{\prod_{g,t}x_{gt}!}
   \prod_{g,t}w_{gt}(\eta)^{x_{gt}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Likewise, the saved length is zero outside \(\mathcal B_K\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
L-R_a(\eta)
 &=\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p^{\mathrm{save}}_{a,j}(\eta),\\
p^{\mathrm{save}}_{a,j}(\eta)
 &=\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_K}
   \bigl[L-\ell(a(x))\bigr]
   \frac{\kappa^{|x|}}{\prod_{g,t}x_{gt}!}
   \prod_{g,t}w_{gt}(\eta)^{x_{gt}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The second polynomial does not actually depend on \(j\), but retaining the index makes the closure argument uniform.  In both displays the \(p\)'s are polynomials over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).  For \(\bullet\in\{\mathrm{fail},\mathrm{save}\}\), define on all of \(\mathcal N\)
\[
F^{\bullet}_j(\eta)
=\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p^{\bullet}_{a,j}(\eta).
\]
This is continuous, so its restriction to \(\overline S_j\) is a continuous extension of the corresponding stratum formula.  The extension is profile-specific: at a membership boundary, the original failure table on the boundary stratum can differ from the one-sided table encoded by an adjacent \(F^{\mathrm{fail}}_j\).

Apply the cited compatible-stratification result once more to the finite family of compact semialgebraic closures \(\overline S_j\).  Denote the resulting smooth strata within \(\overline S_j\) by \(R_{jr}\).  On such a stratum, put \(F=\exp\{-\kappa M\}p\), where \(p\) is either polynomial belonging to the fixed closure continuation.  For \(\eta\in R_{jr}\) and \(u\in T_\eta R_{jr}\), the chain and product rules give
\[
dF_\eta(u)
=\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}
 \bigl(dp_\eta(u)-\kappa p(\eta)dM_\eta(u)\bigr).
\]
The exponential factor is strictly positive.  Hence any local extremum of \(F\) relative to \(R_{jr}\) belongs to
\[
\mathcal C_{jr}(p)
=\left\{\eta\in R_{jr}:
  (dp-\kappa p\,dM)_\eta(u)=0
  \text{ for every }u\in T_\eta R_{jr}\right\}.
\]
For a zero-dimensional stratum this condition is vacuous, as it must be.

On each rank-constant chart of a smooth semialgebraic stratum, membership of \(u\) in \(T_\eta R_{jr}\) is expressed by the polynomial Jacobian equations for that chart; partitioning by the finitely many relevant nonzero minors shows that the tangent bundle is semialgebraic over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).  The covector \(dp-\kappa p\,dM\) also has polynomial coefficients over this field.  Thus \(\mathcal C_{jr}(p)\) is semialgebraic over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\): its complement is the projection of the semialgebraic set of pairs \((\eta,u)\) for which \(u\in T_\eta R_{jr}\) and the displayed covector is nonzero on \(u\), and projection and complementation preserve semialgebraicity.  By the cited finiteness result, each \(\mathcal C_{jr}(p)\) has finitely many connected components.

The function \(F\) is constant on every such connected component.  Indeed, the cited path result joins any two points of a component by a semialgebraic path \(\gamma\) that is continuously differentiable on finitely many pieces.  On every differentiable piece,
\[
\frac{d}{dt}F(\gamma(t))
=\exp\{-\kappa M(\gamma(t))\}
 (dp-\kappa p\,dM)_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))
=0.
\]
The fundamental theorem of calculus on each piece and continuity at the finitely many joins prove constancy.

Each continuation attains its minimum and maximum on the compact set \(\overline S_j\).  If \(\eta_\star\) is such an extremizer and lies in \(R_{jr}\), then it is also a local extremum relative to \(R_{jr}\), so \(\eta_\star\in\mathcal C_{jr}(p)\).  It follows that every closure-extremum value is the constant value of one of the finitely many critical components just constructed.

We next prove the asserted algebraic-representative property.  First, every nonempty semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R^d\) defined over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) contains a point in \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^d\).  For \(d=1\), a quantifier-free description uses finitely many polynomials over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\); their real roots are algebraic, and every complementary sign interval contains a rational point.  For \(d>1\), project onto the first coordinate.  The cited projection theorem and the one-dimensional case supply an algebraic first coordinate in the projection.  The corresponding nonempty fiber is semialgebraic over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\), and induction supplies the remaining algebraic coordinates.

Now let \(C\) be a connected component of some \(\mathcal C_{jr}(p)\).  Connected components are closed, and there are finitely many of them; hence \(C\) is also relatively open in \(\mathcal C_{jr}(p)\).  For any \(z\in C\), choose a rational open box \(V\) containing \(z\) such that
\[
\varnothing\ne V\cap\mathcal C_{jr}(p)\subseteq C.
\]
The intersection on the left is semialgebraic over \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\), so the preceding paragraph gives an algebraic point \(\eta_C\in C\).

It remains to relate the closure continuations to the original piecewise functions.  Because \(S_j\) is dense in \(\overline S_j\) and \(F^{\bullet}_j\) is continuous,
\[
\inf_{\eta\in S_j}F^{\bullet}_j(\eta)
=\min_{\eta\in\overline S_j}F^{\bullet}_j(\eta),
\qquad
\sup_{\eta\in S_j}F^{\bullet}_j(\eta)
=\max_{\eta\in\overline S_j}F^{\bullet}_j(\eta).
\]
Since the finitely many \(S_j\) partition \(\mathcal N\), the coverage identities are therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\inf_{\eta\in\mathcal N}Q_a(\eta)
 &=\min_j\left\{1-max_{\eta\in\overline S_j}
                         F^{\mathrm{fail}}_j(\eta)\right\},\\
\sup_{\eta\in\mathcal N}Q_a(\eta)
 &=\max_j\left\{1-min_{\eta\in\overline S_j}
                         F^{\mathrm{fail}}_j(\eta)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Similarly,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\inf_{\eta\in\mathcal N}R_a(\eta)
 &=\min_j\left\{L-max_{\eta\in\overline S_j}
                         F^{\mathrm{save}}_j(\eta)\right\},\\
\sup_{\eta\in\mathcal N}R_a(\eta)
 &=\max_j\left\{L-min_{\eta\in\overline S_j}
                         F^{\mathrm{save}}_j(\eta)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
These equalities do not assert that the original piecewise function attains an extremum.  If an adjacent membership table changes from failure to coverage at a boundary, the appropriate closure value is exactly its unattained one-sided limit, and the formulas still include it.

Finally, at every algebraic representative \(\eta_C\), both \(M(\eta_C)\) and \(p(\eta_C)\) are algebraic.  Isolating intervals and rational directed rounding give arbitrarily narrow rational enclosures for them.  To enclose the remaining exponential, choose a rational \(Q>|z|\), where \(z=-\kappa M(\eta_C)\), and an integer \(m\ge Q\).  Taylor's formula gives
\[
\exp(z)=\sum_{q=0}^{n}\frac{z^q}{q!}+R_{n+1}(z),
\qquad
|R_{n+1}(z)|
\le 3^m\frac{Q^{n+1}}{(n+1)!},
\]
because \(\exp(Q)\le\exp(m)<3^m\); the rational bound tends to zero as \(n\to\infty\).  Combining it with shrinking algebraic isolating intervals produces convergent rational outward enclosures for every component value \(\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta_C)\}p(\eta_C)\).  There are finitely many component values.  Whenever a comparison of a global coverage or risk extremum with a rational threshold is strict, the finite candidate set has a positive separation from that threshold on the required side, so sufficiently refined outward enclosures certify the comparison.  At equality the intervals need not separate, and no termination claim is made.  This proves the corrected statement.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(s\in\mathcal S_T\) with real-algebraic coordinates, a positive real-algebraic \(\kappa\), an integer \(K\in\mathbb N_0\), and a finite endpoint grid \(\mathcal G_h\subset\Theta\) consisting of real-algebraic points. Let \(a\) be a complete profile assigning a closed endpoint-grid interval to every \(x\in\mathcal B_K\) and assigning \(\Theta\) outside \(\mathcal B_K\). Put \(Q_a(\eta)=P_{\eta,\kappa}\{\theta(\eta)\in a(X)\}\) and \(R_a(\eta)=\mathbb E_{P_{\eta,\kappa}}[\ell(a(X))]\). There is a finite smooth semialgebraic stratification \(\{S_j\}\) of the compact nuisance box, compatible with its boundary and all target-membership relations, such that on every \(S_j\)
\[
Q_a(\eta)=1-\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p^{\mathrm{fail}}_{a,j}(\eta),
\qquad
L-R_a(\eta)=\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p^{\mathrm{save}}_{a,j}(\eta),
\]
where the two \(p\)'s are polynomials over the real algebraic numbers. Each displayed exponential--polynomial has a continuous extension to \(\overline S_j\). For finite compatible smooth semialgebraic stratifications of all the closures \(\overline S_j\), every minimum or maximum of every continuation is the value on a connected component of the tangential critical locus
\[
dp-\kappa p\,dM=0.
\]
There are finitely many such components, the continuation is constant on each component, and every component contains a real-algebraic representative. The global infimum and supremum of each original, possibly discontinuous, piecewise function \(Q_a\) and \(R_a\) are affine transforms of extrema of these closure continuations. Thus the finite candidate set includes any unattained one-sided boundary limit caused by a table switching between failure and coverage. Convergent rational outward algebraic--exponential enclosures decide every strict rational comparison with these global extrema; no decision claim is made for equality contacts.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim incorrectly treats total coverage itself as one exponential--polynomial surface and can be read as asserting attainment despite closed-interval membership jumps. The corrected claim states the exact failure and saved-length formulas, optimizes their continuous stratum-closure continuations, and includes unattained one-sided limits while limiting algorithmic decidability to strict comparisons.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(s\in\mathcal S_T\) with real-algebraic coordinates, a positive real-algebraic \(\kappa\), an integer \(K\in\mathbb N_0\), and a finite endpoint grid \(\mathcal G_h\subset\Theta\) consisting of real-algebraic points. Let \(a\) be a complete profile assigning a closed endpoint-grid interval to every \(x\in\mathcal B_K\) and assigning \(\Theta\) outside \(\mathcal B_K\). Put \(Q_a(\eta)=P_{\eta,\kappa}\{\theta(\eta)\in a(X)\}\) and \(R_a(\eta)=\mathbb E_{P_{\eta,\kappa}}[\ell(a(X))]\). There is a finite smooth semialgebraic stratification \(\{S_j\}\) of the compact nuisance box, compatible with its boundary and all target-membership relations, such that on every \(S_j\)
\[
Q_a(\eta)=1-\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p^{\mathrm{fail}}_{a,j}(\eta),
\qquad
L-R_a(\eta)=\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p^{\mathrm{save}}_{a,j}(\eta),
\]
where the two \(p\)'s are polynomials over the real algebraic numbers. Each displayed exponential--polynomial has a continuous extension to \(\overline S_j\). For finite compatible smooth semialgebraic stratifications of all the closures \(\overline S_j\), every minimum or maximum of every continuation is the value on a connected component of the tangential critical locus
\[
dp-\kappa p\,dM=0.
\]
There are finitely many such components, the continuation is constant on each component, and every component contains a real-algebraic representative. The global infimum and supremum of each original, possibly discontinuous, piecewise function \(Q_a\) and \(R_a\) are affine transforms of extrema of these closure continuations. Thus the finite candidate set includes any unattained one-sided boundary limit caused by a table switching between failure and coverage. Convergent rational outward algebraic--exponential enclosures decide every strict rational comparison with these global extrema; no decision claim is made for equality contacts.
proposed.justification: At each algebraic observed design this converts continuum nuisance optimization into finitely many closure-continuation critical values without confusing coverage with failure probability or assuming boundary attainment.
proposed.gap: The Poisson likelihood makes the exponential factor cancel from the tangential critical equation, but exact equality contacts remain undecidable by interval separation and their uniform variation over shares and intensity is not resolved here.
proposed.consumer: A verified fixed-design solver may enclose finitely many algebraically represented critical-component values and certify strict global coverage or risk comparisons, including one-sided membership-switch limits.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the claim and dependency metadata atomically so the proof uses the declared box assumptions and the frozen cited semialgebraic theorem, and so downstream certificate work receives the corrected closure-continuation result.

prose_updates.tldr: A staggered multiplicative panel with rare Poisson totals turns the Moreau--Kastler equation (3.14) proportional-effect setup into a discrete minimax confidence problem. The contribution derives the exact low-intensity deterministic value and all optimizers, proves a strict first-order gain from randomized interval kernels, prices the stronger all-untreated-zero fallback separately, and relates both procedures to the efficient high-intensity Gaussian limit. At every fixed algebraic observed design, failure probability and saved length are exponential--polynomial on target-membership strata; continuous extensions to the compact stratum closures reduce all extrema and one-sided limits to finitely many algebraically represented critical-component values, so strict rational comparisons terminate. The remaining open theorem asks for a uniform finite machine representation across shares and compact intensity ranges, including exact coverage contacts and the mandatory \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), \(K=2\), \(h=.01\) certificate with gap at most \(.05\).

project_justification.gap: Regular staggered-PPML work supplies the proportional target and high-information inference, while exact discrete interval work treats scalar families or finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations. Existing results do not convert fixed-design strict exponential--polynomial comparisons into a terminating rational-polyhedral cover that remains valid at nominal-coverage and target-endpoint contacts uniformly over observed shares and compact intensity ranges.
project_justification.fill: The paper joins exact low-count values and a high-count efficiency bridge to a rigorous fixed-algebraic-design reduction: stratum-closure continuations capture attained extrema and unattained membership-switch limits through finitely many critical components. It also specifies a finite certificate format whose accepted rational data would prove global coverage, conservative upper risk, and an integrality-preserving lower bound with an explicit error ledger; existence and synthesis of that uniform certificate remain the stated open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), supplies the imputed counterfactual-share proportional target; that algebraic specialization is setup rather than a novel theorem here. Wooldridge (2023) identifies staggered nonlinear cohort-time effects and makes pooled Poisson quasi-likelihood operational under fixed \(T\), while Martin (2017), Theorems 1--2, establishes regular fixed-\(T\) asymptotics for multiplicative-panel averages; both inform the high-information endpoint. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005), Theorem 1, supplies Bayes--minimax duality but does not calculate this multivariate connected-interval game. Kabaila and Byrne (2001) supply the ordered scalar exact-Poisson benchmark and the homogeneous known-mass reduction is only a sanity check. Kabaila (2013) supplies auxiliary-uniform atom splitting, and Habiger, McCann, and Tebbs (2013) studies integrated one-parameter discrete optimality. Bochnak, Coste, and Roy (1998) supply the classical semialgebraic projection, compatible-stratification, finite-component, and path facts used by the fixed-design reduction; the Poisson critical-equation cancellation and the treatment of discontinuous membership boundaries are derived here. Schafer and Stark (2009), especially Theorem 6 and the Conclusion, establish finite-prior Monte Carlo convergence and off-support risk control, but not a deterministic stopping rule, global continuum honesty, or a complete integer lower certificate. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, characterize uniform asymptotic size through drifting subsequences, but do not provide finite rational cells, computable outward enclosures, or a terminating acceptance predicate. The open certificate question is stated as a strict finite verified strengthening of these last two guarantees. Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), Theorems 1 and 3, informs the Poisson--Gaussian comparison without itself profiling this causal nuisance or transferring the connected-interval minimax game.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-design result does not claim that total coverage is one exponential--polynomial, that the discontinuous piecewise coverage function attains its extrema, or that equality contacts are decidable. It instead optimizes continuous fixed-profile extensions on compact stratum closures and includes unattained one-sided membership-switch limits; outward enclosures terminate only for strict rational comparisons. Uniformly parameterizing those contacts over the full observed-share simplex and compact intensity ranges remains open. The mandatory early-kill instance is \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), count box \(K=2\), and endpoint mesh \(.01\): it still requires an accepted globally share-uniform deterministic primal and a complete integer lower certificate with gap at most \(.05\). A nuisance grid, sampled-share check, fixed-share certificate, root linear-programming relaxation, or unbudgeted numerical gap does not pass.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal-functional identity is setup credited to Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), and the homogeneous known-mass scalar reduction is a sanity check credited to Kabaila and Byrne (2001). The independent Poisson total law and share lower bound define the experiment; the exposure, time-effect, treatment-effect, and calibrated known-intensity restrictions are maintained rather than consequences of PPML theory. The fixed-algebraic-design separation result covers strict comparisons of closure-continuation extrema and one-sided limits, not exact equality contacts or a uniform finite cover. The latter remains an open-ended certificate question, including the early-kill construction. An unknown or estimated intensity changes the experiment and remains unsolved. No claim is made for noninteger outcomes, arbitrary overdispersion, individual-data sufficiency, or software-default intervals. The exact positive-intensity randomized value away from the low-count phase and the global closed-form maximizer of \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) are outside the promised theorem spine unless they emerge from the certificate analysis.

statement_notes.justification: At each algebraic observed design this gives a finite, rigorous nuisance-optimization reduction while retaining discontinuous membership-switch limits.
statement_notes.gap: The exponential cancels from tangential critical equations, but outward intervals decide only strict comparisons; equality contacts and their uniform share--intensity parameterization remain outside the lemma.
statement_notes.consumer: Verified fixed-design solvers can enclose finitely many algebraically represented component values and certify strict global coverage or risk comparisons without nuisance sampling or a false attainment claim.
